details.contract:
manifest: add path: { type: "string" } to the input table. Leave the description prose byte-identical (TOOLS-SPEC.md's text is asserted by tests; the docs task rewrites it).

handler:
- pass { kinds: args.kinds, path: args.path } to resolve(); TraceArgs gains the field.
- ambiguous payload gains candidates_total and candidates_shown straight from the Resolution; totals.candidates_total becomes candidates_total and a new totals.candidates_shown is added. One number per name: the summary line must agree with candidates_total.
- every candidate gains next_call: { tool: "trace", query: <candidate.qn>, direction: <args.direction ?? "all"> }.
- not_found near misses gain the same next_call shape.

Do not change direction/kinds/depth semantics, budgets, or the candidate score model.
A filtered not_found must stay not_found, and its near misses must already be path-filtered by resolve.

details.contract:
payload.unresolved entries gain bucket: UnresolvedBucket from bucketOf(row) in #shared/domain/unresolved.ts.

New argument: unresolved: { type: "enum", values: [...UNRESOLVED_BUCKETS] } — imported from #shared/domain/unresolved.ts, never restated. When present it filters the listed rows to that bucket only.

New payload key: unresolved_census = { total, material, buckets } from bucketCensus(rows) over the SAME rows the answer's coverage.unresolved_edges was computed from, so total === coverage.unresolved_edges in every answer. It describes the unfiltered scope even when the unresolved argument filters the list.

When the filter is active, the summary line says how many were filtered out, so a short list never reads as a complete one.

Do not change coverage.unresolved_edges, its meaning, or its role in total_relation. Do not rename existing unresolved entry keys (file, line, name, evidence, tier).

details.contract:
New argument: range: { type: "array", items: { type: "integer" } } — exactly two integers, [from, to], 1-based inclusive, meaningful only with what=source.

Behaviour: clamp to the resolved node's own extent [startLine, endLine]; never throw for an out-of-extent or inverted range. from is clamped into [startLine, endLine]; to is clamped into [from, endLine]. The payload keeps a single effective window (the existing SourcePayload.window), and why names the clamp when it happened — for example "range clamped to the node's extent 12-40" — so the caller sees that the request was narrowed instead of silently answered.

New what value: "outline". Payload: { target, what: "outline", why, path, members: [{ qn, kind, lines: [start, end], signature }] } built from reader.members(node.id) for a class-like node and reader.nodesByFile(node.fileId) for a file node, in source order. No new reader method, no new query.

If argument parsing does not already coerce array items to integers, extend src/shared/cli/args.ts for the declared items type inside this task; the manifest table stays the source of truth.
Do not change the window semantics for a plain what=source call, and do not touch source_drift.
details.goal: expand what=source can be narrowed to a caller-chosen sub-span, and a new what=outline returns a file or class member list with signatures and line numbers.
steps: Add range and the outline value to the manifest, plus any parser support the integer item type needs in src/shared/cli/args.ts.
Implement range clamping in the source branch, keeping window as the single effective span and stating the clamp in why.
Implement the outline branch over members()/nodesByFile().

Extend tests/tools-expand.test.ts: a range inside the node returns exactly those lines; a range crossing the node boundary is clamped and why says so; an inverted range yields an empty window without throwing; outline returns members in source order with signature and lines.
Run the task verification against this repository: expand AGENTS.md --what outline, then expand AGENTS.md --what source --range 1:5.

~/.bun/bin/bun run test tests/tools-expand.test.ts tests/cli-args.test.ts  (all pass)
